claims.text: Its AI customer ARR reached $234M in Q2 2026, up 212% year over year.
DigitalOcean reported $281M in second-quarter 2026 revenue, up 29%, and raised its 2026 guidance to $1.17B to $1.18B.
AI customer ARR reached $234M, and the company says 85% of it comes from inference and core cloud rather than bare metal.
Remaining performance obligations rose to $894M, including its first nine-figure annual customer commitments.
It has about 155 MW of committed data center capacity, including 20 MW added for 2027 and 2028.
A follow-on share offering in the first quarter of 2026 raised $888M net, and it used $500M of that to repay debt.
CEO Paddy Srinivasan expects growth to reach 35% or more by the fourth quarter of 2026 and to exceed 50% in 2027.
Third-quarter guidance is $304M to $307M.
The company is moving from small monthly accounts toward large AI contracts, and its weighted average contract life has risen from 1.6 years to more than 3 years.

claims.text: It reported more than US$10M of ARR in April 2026 and has reserved about 1 GW in Alberta.
The Logic reported in April 2026 that Denvr had raised US$12.5M of equity, deployed about US$100M of infrastructure on its own account and passed US$10M of ARR.
It runs a facility in southeast Calgary and has reserved about 1 GW of capacity across two Alberta sites that it has not fully built.
The company competes for Canadian federal and Alberta government work in defence, health and sovereignty, and planned to add infrastructure later in 2026.
Denvr plans to grow in modular blocks of 1 MW to 5 MW and to bid for Canadian sovereign and defence AI work with partners in its CAIP Defence Coalition.

claims.text: In April 2024 Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry certified the group's plan to supply H200 cloud capacity under its economic security cloud program, with a subsidy of up to ¥1.925B toward a build of about ¥10B.
GMO Internet, Inc., the Tokyo-listed group company that took over the infrastructure business in January 2025, runs the service.
